chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has two wives and wishes to favor one of them with clothing and a gift; is that permissible? He said: There is no harm in that, but strive for justice between them.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a husband to give more gifts to one wife than the other?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that while material inequality in gifts (*kiswa*) and stipends (*atiyya*) is permissible, it must be grounded in sincere effort (*ijtihad*) toward fairness rather than absolute mathematical equality. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic view that 'justice' in polygyny allows for discretionary favor in non-mandatory aspects, provided the husband does not neglect his duty of equitable treatment. The ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic injunctions on marital conduct within the domestic sphere.
